name: Marawan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct, poorly attested Arawakan; Glottolog lists no Glottolog's most extensive description references at all (only Rivet & Reinburg 1921 mention).

sources.citation: A obra linguística de Curt Nimuendaju (facsimile ed. 1999), entry XII on Nimuendajú, Curt. 1926. Die Palikur-Indianer und ihre Nachbarn. Göteborgs Kungl. Vetenskaps- och Vitterhets-Samhälles Handlingar 31(2).

sources.note: Reports that Nimuendajú 1926 contains a Palikur vocabulary (pp. 127-140) with a note on diacritics, and 'finalmente Maraon com 2 itens apenas (144)' -- a two-item Maraon list, so it cannot carry a Marawan stress statement.

sources.note: Nothing. Lists Marawan/Maraon (Oiapoque and Curipi rivers) with the single source 'Reinburg in Rivet and Reinburg 1921, pp. 110-111', plus Caripurá (Faria ms.) and Palicur; six-word comparative table (pi-tiui, pi-taibi, pu-aku, uni, tiketi, kamui) without accent marks.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & P. Reinburg. 1921. Les Indiens Marawan. Journal de la Société des Américanistes 13(1): 103-118. DOI 10.3406/jsa.1921.2907.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only primary document on the language: a c. 70-item wordlist taken in 1916 at St-Georges de l'Oyapock (pp. 110-111), ethnographic notes (pp. 103-106), Arawak affiliation and a comparative vocabulary (pp. 106-118). The authors write, p. 108: 'Les documents marawan que nous avons examinés sont trop brefs pour permettre une étude de phonétique comparée' and note only one consonant correspondence (t ~ s/x/h/y/k, p. 109). No word 'accent' anywhere; the Marawan column carries macron/tilde vowel marks only (kutru, pi-taïbi, ï-tsââlo, pânuku), no stress marks. Persée's PDF download is be…
